feedback: Written before this candidate has raced; no outcome is claimed for it. Evidence from iteration 5 (y 0.08, wheel_track 0.12, score 561.6): the oval finished 20 of 20 with oscillation 0.20, the s-bend finished 11 of 20 with 9 off-track exits, max_error 0.047 and control_effort 12.2 (the highest of any track), and the slalom finished 0 of 20 with line_loss 1.35. The lookahead sweep (iterations 3, 1, 4, 5) is monotone, so lookahead is no longer the lever. Your proposed wheel_track 0.10 is physically sound: turn rate is the wheel speed difference divided by wheel_track, so the narrower track adds yaw per unit of steering command, and this corrects the wheel_track 0.14 advice I gave earlier. Next race: if s-bend off-track exits fall below 9 of 20 and control_effort falls from 12.2 while the oval finish stays at or near 1.0 and oscillation stays below about 0.4, keep wheel_track 0.10 and try the first requested change. If oscillation rises above about 0.4 or the oval finish falls below 0.85, the extra yaw gain is too high, so try the second change. If slalom line_loss stays at about 1.3 or above with the track fixed, try the third change.
requested_changes: If the s-bend off-track exits fall with steering_oscillation below about 0.4 at wheel_track 0.10, keep y 0.08 and hold wheel_track at 0.10 as the new best track width. Evidence: iteration 5 s-bend control_effort was 12.2 with 9 of 20 off-track exits, and a narrower track adds yaw per PWM count, so it should reduce the effort needed in bends.

If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.4 or the oval finish falls below 0.85 at wheel_track 0.10, try wheel_track 0.11 as a compromise, or keep wheel_track 0.10 and lower kp to 3.5 to cancel the extra yaw gain. Evidence: iteration 5 oscillation was 0.20 on the oval and 0.32 on the s-bend at wheel_track 0.12, so the gain increase should be moved in small steps.

If slalom line_loss_events stay at about 1.3 or above with the track fixed, do not widen the sensor span beyond x ±0.024. Evidence: iteration 2 at ±0.032 with kp 4.5 cut the oval finish to 8 of 20 and did not fix the bends. Instead, test a 12 mm footprint at the same ±0.024 x positions, since iteration 0 (12 mm, y 0.06) had line_loss 1.9 on slalom and that was the worst value, so this should be treated as a test rather than an expected fix.
